tweets.text:
Today I figured out what "AI vibe coding" means as a product manager.

And it was thanks to @boltdotnew⚡️ 

Vibe coding is iterating on an idea **without thinking about the tool.**

When coding software is as easy as: 
• Finessing a tweet
• Tweaking the timing in iMovie
• Expressing knowledge in Notion

All I think about is **what I want to try** and **how does the result feel.** 
(Not: lots of clicks, dead ends, or web searches)

What happened: 
⮑ Brushing my teeth this morning I had an idea for a tool to give context and nuance to cherry-picked sound bites. 
⮑ On my walk to work I talked to Claude and workshopped it down to an MVP 
⮑ I asked Claude for a prompt for Bolt, and before I finished my coffee it was working (including API calls to o3-mini).

I spent a few more hours, but it wasn't debugging—it was **playing.** The "work" was applying taste: getting a sense for the output & iterating on what I actually wanted. 

Since childhood I've been keeping a list of tools that inspired me to create. Today Bolt officially joins that list:
🎥 iMovie 

🎨 Canva 

🎛️ Garageband 

🏎️ LEGO mindstorms robotics

🤓 Django/Meteor/Glitch

✍️ Notion

🎙️ Riverside (why I joined!) 

⚡️ Bolt (welcome to the hall of fame!)

Product managers: I recommend trying Bolt for a standalone idea, so you can get a sense of what it's like to think without babysitting a tool. It's ideal for iterating on experiences that are more about the content or data.

Engineers: I love coding; it is its own kind of flow. But it's not the kind of flow that alone leads to amazing products. AI prototyping lets you wear your product hat and apply your taste more often.

🔴 PS if you found this valuable, I'm hosting a free live demo "Build 6 PM AI Agents in 56 minutes" https://t.co/2WzUQJfydK with leaders from Relay, Zapier, and Lindy (if you can't make it sign up and I'll send out the recording after)
